resources.string: Talk on your iPhone

Hear calls and talk with your iPhone’s own microphone and speaker. Android keeps call audio away from apps, so this needs Shizuku, a free app that gives Pairline extra access with your permission. Both phones also need to be on the same Wi-Fi.

Talk on iPhone
What is Shizuku? Does it need root?

Shizuku is a free, open-source app that lends Pairline the rights of Android’s own debugging tool, with your permission. No root is needed. Pairline uses it only to carry call audio and for the call keypad, mute and speaker. You can take the permission back in Shizuku at any time.
Why does call audio go back to this phone after a restart?

Android turns Wireless debugging off every time the phone restarts, and that stops Shizuku. Pairline then shows a notification: tap it and start Shizuku again, and calls play on your iPhone again. Until then calls still ring and work on the iPhone, with the audio on this phone. On a rooted phone Shizuku can start by itself.
An app complains that debugging is on

Some banking and payment apps refuse to open while Developer options or Wireless debugging are on. Pairline never turns them on by itself. Turn Wireless debugging off while you use such an app; Shizuku may stop, and you start it again later for call audio.
I hear calls on the iPhone, but they can’t hear me

Some phones don’t let any app feed audio into a call. Then you hear calls on the iPhone and talk on this phone. After each call the iPhone asks how it sounded; your answers help Pairline try another way on the next call.
